findings.citation: A. Addazi, J. Alvarez-Muniz, R. Alves Batista, G. Amelino-Camelia et al. (162 authors), "Quantum gravity phenomenology at the dawn of the multi-messenger era—A review", Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys. 125 (2022) 103948, arXiv:2111.05659 (journal)
findings.summary: The closing summary of the review's section 2 lists, among the observable hallmarks of Born geometry and metastring theory, "a 'dual' geometry, leading to dark energy in the observed spacetime, modelled as a positive cosmological constant", citing Berglund–Hübsch–Minić 2019 (PLB 798; IJMPD 28). A restatement of the claim g4 rated partial for C5 (BHM 2019: the curvature of the canonically conjugate dual space induces our dark energy), placed in a widely cited review.
findings.difference: Same gap as its sources: our dark energy is the static curvature of the dual (canonically conjugate) spacetime, modelled as a positive Λ; no collapse or contraction of the dual side, no a·ã = 1 and no w_eff = −w̃ dictionary. One summary sentence without derivation: it adds circulation, not independent prior art beyond BHM 2019. If the collapse is read as the conjecture's core, the label would be 'related'.

findings.citation: T. Hübsch, D. Minic, "Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory", arXiv:2610.19522 (2026); arXiv preprint only
findings.summary: The newest statement (October 2026) of the Minic group's dark-energy claim: "curvature of dual spacetime can lead to a dynamical origin of dark energy", citing BHM 2019 (PLB 798), BHM 2021 (LHEP 186) and Hur et al. 2025 (JCAP 11, 054), and the observed vacuum-energy scale "dynamically associated (from the metastring point of view) with the geometry of dual spacetime". Same claim g4 rated partial in BHM 2019 and Hur et al. 2025.
findings.difference: Hedged ('can lead to') and not developed here. Dark energy from the dual spacetime's curvature, not from the collapse of a contracting conjugate universe; no a·ã = 1, no w_eff = −w̃ dictionary, no stiff content. Adds no independent prior art beyond its cited sources; shows the claim is current.

findings.citation: T. Hübsch, D. Minic, "Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory", arXiv:2610.19522 (2026); arXiv preprint only
findings.summary: Outside this list's named conjectures (C5–C7). States that for each field φ_λ(x, x̃) there is a dual field which, after integration over the dual spacetime label, "is a candidate for the invisible matter sector (dual to the observed, visible, Standard Model sector)", and that the classical spacetime label x of canonical QFT represents "a choice of (classical spacetime) polarization in modular (quantum) spacetime". A restatement, citing Minic 2020 and BHM 2021 (LHEP), of the claim g1 rated 'anticipates' in those papers and in Hübsch–Minic 2026 (arXiv:2604.19418).
findings.difference: Metastring framework: the dark sector is made of dual fields that do not commute with the visible fields, rather than the same fields in the mirror polarization; hedged as a 'candidate'; no velocity gate, monopoles or kinematics of momentum-polarized matter. Its polarization language is close to the program's (#11 §3–§4). Not independent of the group's earlier statements.

findings.citation: H. Falomir, J. Gamboa, P. Gondolo, F. Méndez, "Magnetic Seed and Cosmology as Quantum Hall Effect", Phys. Lett. B 785 (2018) 399, arXiv:1801.07575 (journal)
findings.summary: Two metric sectors with scale factors a(t) and b(t) whose minisuperspace momenta do not commute ([π₁, π₂] = εθ), an interaction read as "a relic of a causal primordial connection between sectors". The coupling terms in each sector's Friedmann equations "can be considered as sources of dark energy"; for Λ₂ = 0 the component is a generalized Chaplygin gas. A second sector's dynamics acting on our expansion as dark energy is C5's theme. Companion of Falomir et al. 2017 (arXiv:1707.04670), which g4 rated related.
findings.difference: The second sector is a separate spacetime region ('patch'), not the conjugate (momentum-space) description of our universe; the coupling is a noncommutative deformation of the scale factors' momenta, not Born reciprocity; nothing says the other sector contracts or collapses; no a·ã = 1, no w_eff = −w̃ dictionary, no Λ from dual kinetic energy.

findings.citation: A. Ghosh, D. S. Ray, "Born-Kothari condensation in an ideal Fermi gas", Phys. Rev. A 95 (2017) 022129, doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.95.022129 (journal; not on arXiv)
findings.summary: Re-examines Kothari and Nath's 1943 'condensation' in Fermi–Dirac statistics, which the abstract calls a natural consequence of Born's reciprocity principle (Born 1938), and gives it a symmetry-breaking order parameter as condensation-like coherence in an ideal Fermi gas. With the companion review (recid:1625396), a Born-reciprocity-derived concentration of matter at the top of a bounded momentum space.
findings.difference: A quantum-statistical effect of an ideal gas with a maximum momentum: no interaction, attraction, gravity or instability, no dark matter, no streams of particles sharing a velocity. C6 is collective clumping of dark matter in velocity space by a velocity-gated attraction, the Jeans problem with x and v exchanged. Shared only: matter concentrating in momentum space, derived from Born reciprocity. Verdict rests on the abstract; the paywalled full text was not read.

it is possible to associate an intrinsic notion of symmetry breaking and the thermodynamic

findings.citation: A. Ghosh, "Born-Kothari Condensation for Fermions", Entropy 19 (2017) 479, doi:10.3390/e19090479 (journal mini-review; not on arXiv)
findings.summary: Mini-review of the same work (recid:1515614): for fermions the condensed phase is single-occupancy dense modes at the highest energy state, and the highest momentum of individual fermions, prerequisite for the condensation, is fixed by the problem's natural length and energy scales. This locates Born–Kothari condensation in momentum space, at its upper bound.
findings.difference: As for recid:1515614: an ideal-gas statistical effect at a momentum cutoff, with no dark matter, attraction, instability or velocity streams. Verdict rests on the INSPIRE abstract; the MDPI and DOAJ pages returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch.

quotes.text: for fermions, due to Pauli exclusion principle, the condensed phase occurs only in the form of a single occupancy dense modes at the highest energy state
the highest momentum (energy) for individual fermions, prerequisite for the condensation process, can be specified in terms of the natural length and energy scales of the problem

notes: All 65 records got a verdict: 5 'finding' (7 finding entries), 60 'not-relevant', 0 'unavailable'. No record states C5, C6 or C7. Most flags are regex artifacts: 22 of the 27 C6/C7 flags come from 'gated' inside 'investigated', 'conjugated' or 'variegated'; most C5 flags are maximal (proper) acceleration of particles (Caianiello's line), Unruh-type 'accelerated fields', or pc-GR's 'dark energy', a phenomenological fluid that accumulates near masses. The Addazi et al. review was flagged only for 'accelerators' and holds the strongest statement on the list. Findings: (1) two restatements of the Minic group's claims, the Addazi et al. 2022 review (PPNP, 619 citations) and Hübsch–Minic 2026: the dual spacetime's curvature or geometry gives our dark energy (C5 partial, as g4 rated BHM 2019 and Hur et al. 2025; no collapse, contraction or dictionary) and dual fields as the dark sector (C1, outside this list's named conjectures; g1 rated the sources 'anticipates'). They add circulation, not independent prior art. (2) Falomir et al. 2018, C5 related: a second metric sector coupled through noncommuting momenta acts on our Friedmann equation as dark energy, like its 2017 companion. (3) Born–Kothari condensation (Ghosh–Ray 2017; Ghosh 2017), C6 related at low confidence: Born-reciprocity-derived concentration of an ideal Fermi gas at the highest momentum states, with no dark matter, attraction or instability; judged on the INSPIRE abstracts (publisher pages returned 403). Closest not-relevant calls: BHM 2021 (2109.01122) does not attribute Λ to the dual spacetime; Jejjala–Kavic–Minic–Takeuchi 2022 has no dual spacetime; Mantz–Prokopec 2008 (Hermitian gravity) forbids a positive Λ and drives nothing from the momentum side; Artigas–Mielczarek–Rovelli 2019 is minisuperspace recollapse, already the closed-universe note's lead; Hess 2020's 'canonical' acceleration is CCGG gravity. Two records have no abstract anywhere (Brandt 1988, recid:263890; Caianiello 1981, recid:11426); both were judged on their titles plus a companion abstract or citing papers' descriptions, all about maximal particle acceleration. Low 2004 (math-ph/0404077) was read from its PDF. No new leads: Castro Perelman 2020 (recid:1789711), met in a reference list, is on reader r3's list.
